Behind the numbersModel & limitations +

Transparent inputs. Reproducible results.

This is a long-only, fully invested spot portfolio model. All sample allocations, volatilities, correlations and shocks are illustrative. There is no market feed, wallet connection or trading capability.

Scenario return and drawdown
Return = Σ(weight × effective asset shock). Effective shock = entered shock × intensity, floored at −100% per asset. P&L = starting value × return. Drawdown = max(0, −return): a one-step loss, not a historical or simulated peak-to-trough maximum drawdown.
Correlation and volatility
All off-diagonal correlations use one common value ρ between 0 and 1. Annual variance = (1 − ρ)Σ(wᵢσᵢ)² + ρ(Σwᵢσᵢ)². Horizon volatility = annual volatility × √(days / 365). Correlation changes model risk; it does not alter the deterministic scenario return. No simulation is used.
Normal model downside and expected shortfall
Tail-risk measures use stressed horizon volatility only and assume zero expected return with normally distributed returns. Downside at confidence c is the one-sided loss threshold zᶜ × σ; expected shortfall is the average loss conditional on exceeding that threshold, φ(zᶜ) / (1 − c) × σ, so ES ≥ downside. Both are fractions of starting portfolio value. The 95% and 99% values are one-sided, with static positions and common-ρ covariance. Fat tails are likely understated, and deterministic scenario shocks are excluded. The 95% z-score is 1.6448536269514722; the 99% z-score is 2.3263478740408408. These measures are not a maximum loss or a forecast, are not feasible spot-loss bounds, and can exceed 100%.
Reverse stress test
Solves for the instantaneous uniform price shock to the selected assets that reaches a positive target loss in portfolio-percent or USD units. Other assets remain unchanged. Portfolio mode includes stablecoins and cash. This is a long-only spot calculation with a −100% price floor; targets beyond selected exposure are unreachable. It does not depend on correlation, horizon, volatility, shock intensity, or per-asset base shocks. Fees, slippage, liquidity constraints, and price-path effects are excluded. Reverse-stress controls remain in memory for this page session and are not saved.
Concentration
HHI = Σwᵢ². Effective positions = 1 / HHI. The equal-weight comparison assigns 1/N to every listed asset, including any with 0% current weight. Equal weighting is a comparison, not a recommended allocation.
Scope and saved inputs
Asset shocks apply over your chosen scenario event; changing the risk horizon only scales the volatility model, not the shocks. No fees, slippage, liquidity, leverage, liquidation, taxes, rebalancing or intraperiod path effects are modeled. Inputs are saved in this browser’s local storage when available. Export creates a local CSV of assumptions and results.
